paragraphs: Loading timber is a grapple problem. Logs are heavy, round and never the same length, so the crane has to reach, close on an armful and swing it over the bunks in one movement, because doing it twice doubles the cost of every load.

The model holds 217,995 polygons and 208,899 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the crane and trailer can be posed or animated. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits forestry and logistics visualisation, equipment marketing, training material, rural and industrial scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2022.

The M240 is an American designation for a Belgian design that has been in service almost everywhere for decades. It is heavier than the weapons it replaced and universally trusted for exactly that reason: mass is what keeps a machine gun on target.
The model holds 115,113 polygons and 117,077 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 17 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, game weapons, film props, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

Dirt on a crane is honesty. A machine that has been on a site for months carries mud up the tracks, dust on the boom and rust where the paint has gone, and a spotless render of one is the single fastest way to make a construction scene look fake.
The model holds 600,382 polygons and 688,710 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in dirty condition, and carries StemCell certification.
At $79 it suits construction and heavy industry visualisation, equipment marketing, site scenes, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The thobe is a single loose garment from shoulder to ankle, and it is climate engineering as much as clothing: air moves under it, the fabric never touches the skin for long, and the head covering does more work in the sun than any hat would.
The garment holds 64,204 polygons and 127,084 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in brown with the keffiyeh included. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits cultural and regional visualisation, apparel and retail imagery, film and television costume, game characters, education material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A military parachute assembly is two canopies, a harness and a container, packed in an order that a rigger signs for. The reserve is the one that has to work, and everything about how the pack is built is arranged around reaching it quickly.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the backpack and parachute as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 the set suits defence and aviation visualisation, training and safety material, documentary work, film props, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Mining kit is defined by what it has to survive rather than by what it does. Everything is overbuilt, everything is replaceable, and the tools that go underground are chosen because a failure at the face costs a shift rather than a repair.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the equipment as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 the set suits mining and resources visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, documentary work, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A mitre saw is a machine for repeating one cut exactly. The angle is set once and every piece after that matches, which is the entire reason trim carpentry stopped being a craft measured in decades of experience and became something a careful person can do.

The model holds 122,479 polygons and 124,887 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 20 maps, 9 at 4096x4096, 9 at 2048x2048 and 2 smaller. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits tool and equipment marketing, workshop and construction visualisation, retail and e-commerce imagery, training material, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2015.

Laptop design has converged so completely that a generic one is often more useful than any real model. No badge means no dating, no licensing question, and nothing to distract from whatever is meant to be on the screen.
The model holds 134,265 polygons and 144,178 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is enough for close product work. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits product and technology visualisation, interface and screen mockups, office and interior scenes, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Metro rolling stock is designed around the tunnel it runs in rather than around the passenger. The cross section, the door spacing and even the shape of the nose are all dictated by infrastructure that was dug decades before the train was drawn.

The model holds 239,973 polygons and 264,226 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 17 maps, 3 at 4096x4096, 9 at 2048x2048 and 5 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits rail and transport visualisation, urban infrastructure presentation, station scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

Twirling a moustache is shorthand for scheming, and it has been since silent film. On a top hatted businessman mascot it turns a friendly figure into a knowing one, which is exactly the tone most financial and satirical illustration is looking for.
The character is light at 20,199 polygons and 20,478 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in the moustache twirl pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits advertising and mascot work, board game and toy visualisation, editorial and financial illustration, animation and game characters. On sale since 2025.

A disposable anti tank launcher is a tube that is thrown away after one use, and that is the whole design brief. Nothing is maintained, nothing is reloaded, and the weapon is light enough that a soldier will actually carry it before they need it.
The model is light at 41,448 polygons and 43,040 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in new condition. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, game weapons, film props, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A cast is a temporary exoskeleton, and its shape is a clinical decision: how much of the joint above and below to immobilise, where to leave the toes visible, and whether the patient will be allowed to walk on it. Each variation in the collection is a different answer.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the casts as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $79 the set suits medical education and patient explanation, orthopaedic and physiotherapy material, healthcare marketing, character work, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The PKM is the lightest general purpose machine gun of its generation, and the box hanging under it is what makes it a squad weapon rather than a crew served one: the belt is carried by the gun itself, so one soldier can move and fire without help.

The model holds 166,044 polygons and 169,496 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps, 4 at 4096x4096 and 9 at 2048x2048, supplied with the ammunition box. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, game weapons, film props, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

A projected globe is how film and television have shown planetary data since long before anyone could actually build one. It works because a sphere floating in air reads as authoritative, and because a flat map never conveys that something is being watched in real time.
The model holds 117,437 polygons and 121,460 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $79 it suits science fiction film and animation, technology and data visualisation, exhibition and trade show work, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.
